shapes.name: ask-user-question

questions.question: Which events should generate a notification in the first version?

options.label: Assigned to me
options.description: A card/task on the board is assigned or reassigned to the user. Usually the highest-signal trigger and the cheapest to ship first.

options.label: @mentioned in a comment
options.description: Someone names the user in a comment or description. Requires a mention-parsing step, so it carries its own sub-work.

options.label: Activity on my items
options.description: Comments, status changes, or moves on cards the user owns or watches. Highest volume — most likely to need batching or muting.

options.label: Due / overdue
options.description: A card the user owns is approaching its due date or has passed it. Needs a scheduled job rather than an event hook.

questions.question: How should notifications reach the user in v1?

options.label: In-app inbox only
options.description: A bell icon + notification list inside the product. Self-contained, no third-party dependency, ships fastest.

options.label: Email
options.description: Adds an email provider, templating, unsubscribe handling, and deliverability concerns.

options.label: Browser / mobile push
options.description: Real-time pings outside the app. Requires permission prompts, device token storage, and service-worker work.

options.label: Slack
options.description: Post to a DM or channel. Requires an OAuth app install and per-user account linking.

options.label: Real-time per event
options.description: Each trigger fires its own notification immediately. Simplest to build; risks noise on busy boards.

options.label: Real-time in-app, digest elsewhere
options.description: In-app is instant; email/push get rolled up on a schedule. Common pattern, but two delivery paths to build.

options.label: User-configurable preferences
options.description: Per-trigger, per-channel settings plus a digest frequency. Most flexible — adds a whole preferences surface to v1.
